modifications: Entries were selected, normalised (HTML removed, years parsed, headline titles shortened to about 100 characters with an ellipsis), merged and de-duplicated across sources, ranked, capped per day and category, and sorted. Summaries keep the source wording. did_you_know facts are either Wikipedia "Did you know" hooks (text only, reformatted) or one-sentence rewordings of existing entries (prefixed with the date, possibly shortened). Image links are unmodified Wikimedia URLs.

did_you_know.fact: On September 13, 1987: Goiânia accident: A radioactive object is stolen from an abandoned hospital in Goiânia, Brazil, contaminating many people in the following weeks and causing some to die from radiation poisoning.
On September 13, 1962: An appeals court orders the University of Mississippi to admit James Meredith, the first African-American student admitted to the segregated university.
On September 13, 1956: The IBM 305 RAMAC is introduced, the first commercial computer to use disk storage.
On September 13, 1948: Margaret Chase Smith is elected United States senator, and becomes the first woman to serve in both the U.S. House of Representatives and the United States Senate.
September 13 is observed as Roald Dahl Day (Africa, United Kingdom, Latin America).
